_comment: Escapes, early ends and returning villains (Expansion 6 E.4, docs/ADVENTURES.md §5.4; game/story/early.py). `spent`: said when a villain met again before its finale will not run a second time; `escaped`: the journal's line when it got away; `back`: said at the finale of a villain come back from the dead; `relic`: the journal's line when it takes its anchor home. `returning`: a tale forged on a villain come back starts at this attention, and its boss has `hp` more of its hit points for each return (up to `max`). `after`: the days before a contingency's set piece. `kinds`: the short last chapter of each early end (succession: {heir} is the lieutenant who takes its place; cat_away has only `lines`). The relic_moved move is at the end.

spent: {villain_short} does not look for a way out this time. It got away from you once, and it does not mean to run from you again.
There is no breaking off now. {villain_short} has run from you once, and whatever it is, it is too proud to run twice.
This time {villain_short} plants itself and stays. It knows, as you do, that there will be no getting away.
It does not glance at the way out. Whatever let it slip away before, it has spent it, and it knows.
escaped: {villain_short} got away from you, hurt. It will not get away a second time.
It broke off and was gone before you could close. Next time there will be no breaking off.
{villain_short} escaped you once. It cannot do it again: the next meeting ends one way or the other.
It slipped away, bleeding. Whatever trick it used, it has used it.
back: It is the same {villain_short} you put down, and it is not the same: it has come back from that, and it remembers every blow.
You killed {him} once. {villain_short} looks at you across the dark as if to say that it did not take.
{villain_short} has been dead, and is not, and it has had a long time in the dark to think of you.
It knows your face. It came back for it.
relic: {villain_short} has taken what binds {him} out of its hiding place and into {home} itself. If you want it now, you will have to go under {his} roof for it.
Whatever was hidden is hidden no longer: {villain_short} has moved it into {home}, where {he} can watch over it.
The thing you were looking for is gone from where it lay. {villain_short} has carried it home to {home}.
{villain_short} knew you were close. What binds {him} lies in {home} now, under {his} own eye.

title: The Heir
Who Comes After
The Empty Seat
A New Master
goal: {heir} has taken up what {villain_short} left behind. Finish it.
Put an end to {heir}, who sits in {villain_short}'s place now.
Deal with {heir}, the last of {villain_short}'s hands, before {heir} grows into the part.
opening: {villain_short} is dead, but not everything that served {him} died with {him}. {heir} has gathered what was left and gone to ground at {home}, and the word on the road is that {heir} means to carry on.
The news comes within the day: {heir} has taken {villain_short}'s place at {home}, and what was left of {his} following has gone with {heir}. It is smaller now. It will not stay small for long.
Somebody always steps into a dead master's boots. At {home} it is {heir}, and the ones who served {villain_short} serve {heir} now.
{villain_short} fell before {his} time, and left a gap. {heir} has filled it, at {home}, with what was left.
reveal: {heir} is finished, and with {heir} the last of what {villain_short} built.
There is nobody left to take {villain_short}'s place. It is over.
The heir is gone, and there is no other. What {villain_short} began ends here.

title: The Last Order
What It Left Behind
Dead Hands
After the Fall
goal: Live through what {villain_short} set to happen on {his} death.
Come through the last thing {villain_short} arranged for you.
opening: {villain_short} is dead, and you would think it was over. But a thing like {villain_short} does not die without making arrangements, and some of them were for you.
It fell sooner than it meant to. Those who served {him} were told, long ago, what to do if that day came, and the day has come.
Dead, and still not finished with you: {villain_short} left orders, and there are those who mean to carry them out.
{villain_short} planned for its own death, as such things do. Somewhere, something is already on its way to you.
reveal: The last of {villain_short}'s orders is carried out, and failed. There is nothing more behind it.
Whatever {villain_short} left behind, you have lived through it. It is over now.
Its dead hands have reached for you one last time, and missed.

lines: With {villain_short} dead, what {he} held lies open: the way to {home} is clear, and nothing waits there now but what {he} left behind.
The word goes round within the day: {villain_short} is dead, and those who served {him} have scattered. {home} stands empty.
{villain_short} fell before {his} hour, and there is nobody to take {his} place. Its servants are gone like smoke, and {home} lies open to anyone.
Nothing comes after {villain_short}. Its people break and scatter, and {town} breathes again.
